Action Plan:
1. Arrange same-day face-to-face GP appointment for full abdominal and pelvic examination, urinalysis and other indicated tests.  
2. Perform urine β-hCG or serum pregnancy test to rule out early intra-uterine or ectopic pregnancy.  
3. Perform urine dipstick, microscopy/culture ± blood tests (FBE, CRP, renal profile) to assess for urinary tract infection or other inflammatory process.  
4. Provide safety-net advice: if pain worsens, develops syncope, shoulder-tip pain, vomiting, high fever, or any new concerning symptoms, attend ED or call emergency services.  
5. Document amoxicillin allergy in all prescriptions/records.  
6. Follow-up: GP to contact patient with results and management plan; urgent referral to hospital if ectopic pregnancy, PID, appendicitis or other acute abdomen suspected.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 25-year-old female presents with 2-day history of constant dull ache below umbilicus, associated nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.  
• No vomiting, diarrhoea, dysuria, urgency or foul-smelling urine. Reports increased urinary frequency.  
• Mild pink spotting noted in urine stream over last couple of days; expects menstruation soon (LMP ~3 weeks ago). Sexually active with one partner; etonogestrel implant in situ; unsure if pregnant.  
• Constipation one week ago, now resolved; bowel motion yesterday.  
• No vaginal discharge, dyspareunia, light-headedness or fainting.  
Past Medical History: None reported.  
Surgical History: Not mentioned.  
Medications: Etonogestrel implant (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
Allergies: Amoxicillin – allergy (reaction not specified).  
Social: Non-smoker; lives with boyfriend.  
Family History: Brother with type 1 diabetes.

Objective:
• Tele-consult only – no vitals or physical exam performed.  
• No investigations yet performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain with nausea and subjective fever  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Urinary tract infection (cystitis ± early pyelonephritis) – DDx item, High likelihood.  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Early intra-uterine or ectopic pregnancy – DDx Medium (spotting, pain).  
     • Pelvic inflammatory disease – DDx Medium (pain, spotting, fever).  
     • Appendicitis (early/atypical) – DDx Low.  
     • Constipation/functional bowel pain – DDx Low.  
   – Investigations planned: Urine dipstick & culture; serum/urine β-hCG; FBE, CRP; pelvic exam; abdominal examination; consider pelvic ultrasound if pregnancy/ectopic or ovarian pathology suspected.  
   – Treatment planned: Empiric antibiotics only if UTI confirmed; analgesia/antipyretics as needed (avoid amoxicillin-containing regimens).  
   – Relevant referrals: Same-day GP review; urgent hospital referral if ectopic pregnancy, PID or acute abdomen suspected.

2. Pregnancy status uncertainty  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pregnancy status – needs confirmation/exclusion.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Early intra-uterine pregnancy vs ectopic pregnancy (see above).  
   – Investigations planned: Urine or serum pregnancy test; transvaginal ultrasound if positive or high clinical suspicion.  
   – Treatment planned: Based on results; urgent gynecology referral if ectopic suspected.  
   – Relevant referrals: Gynecology/early pregnancy assessment clinic as indicated.

3. Safety-net / escalation advice  
   – Assessment: Risk of deterioration while awaiting evaluation.  
   – Plan: Patient advised to seek immediate medical attention for worsening pain, syncope, vomiting, high fever, shoulder-tip pain, heavy bleeding or other concerns. Documented understanding.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vital signs; no physical abdominal/pelvic exam documented; reaction specifics to amoxicillin not provided; medication dose/route/frequency for implant not specified.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; conversation coherent.
